The 1970 Iñupiaq specimen combines rabbit and wolf skin/fur with yarn, beads and thread; it is not a rabbit-only construction recipe. R65 supplies the separate grouping-of-fingers principle and R66 the worked-skin care comparison. The small thumb-less field pair, its area allocation and useful dry wear are invented limited trials, not a transferred Arctic pattern or a thermal guarantee.
R76 — Fletching, stability and clearance
World Archery: Equipment, arrow section inspected on 25 October 2026; Archery 101: how to fletch an arrow, original coaching article inspected the same day. Supports tail stabilisation, the drag/settling tradeoff and clearance/alignment concerns. Modern plastic vanes, glue, jigs, dimensions and three-vane layout are not adopted. R44 separately supplies bound-vane comparison. The two-feather field lot, two-vane thread attachment and its limited flights are authored, not an experimentally validated reconstruction.
R77 — Wooden utensils and stone-tool woodcarving
National Museum of Denmark: Wooden vessels, institutional account inspected on 25 October 2026, describes Neolithic wood utensils including an oak spoon, elm scoop and alder bowl. Crabtree and Davis, Experimental Manufacture of Wooden Implements with Tools of Flaked Stone, Science 159 (1968), 426–428: indexed abstract inspected the same day; publisher full text is access-blocked. It reports three woodcarving experiments using stone tools, not this spoon’s recipe or labour rate. Later finds establish comparisons, not 40 ka Iberian attestation or a willow food-safety guarantee. The shallow one-piece field spoon remains an authored trial.

09_reference/revision-record.title: Revision Record
09_reference/revision-record.content:
Revision Record
5 October 2026 — skill artwork and Day 40 audit
The artwork commission covers five daily scenes for continuous Days 36–40, Plant-Fibre Clothing and the 29 previously unillustrated skills. The two existing skill plates are retained. Daily scenes use the original Day 1 identity/style reference; manual plates use the original digging-stick style. Geometry references have limited roles. Selected PNGs are copied unchanged, with prompts, rejections and hashes retained in _Artwork/2026-10-05. Mechanical, anatomical or inventory errors are replaced by fresh renders, not cumulative edits. The pre-art notes are archived in _RevisionArchive/2026-10-05-before-skills-and-days-art.zip.
Added Day 40 Technology and Winter Audit and evidence records R27–R32. The comparison separates Palaeolithic working tools from later experiments and dependable seasonal capacity. Month Two Outline now prioritises an enclosed dry sleeping shelter, insulation, food and protected fuel across the remaining work; hunting and firing compete for the same budget. The chronology and limits of the Day 12 eyed needle are clarified. Civilisation Roadmap links the audit. These planning/reference changes add no construction, stock, contact benefit or completed daily event.
This is a dated work record. Counts, folders and descriptions in earlier sections reflect the state at that revision. Category Specification, Topic Index and Dependency Register describe the current organisation.
1 October 2026
The user authorised revision of the setting, style guide, templates, first month, reference dependencies and civilisation roadmap. The original dependency-focused purpose remains central, with narrative used to expose implementation difficulties and local expertise.
A pre-revision archive preserves all 118 original Markdown notes, the old combined context and the two export scripts: _RevisionArchive/2026-10-01-before-revision.zip. This includes the user’s uncommitted note contents; Git history was not used as a substitute for this archive. Obsidian settings were not changed.
Main editorial choices

Retain approximately 40,000 BP and northern Iberia; label the exact valley, weather and encounters as authored choices.
Clarify transit as living-body-only, and provide prior practical training without granting mastery.
Make hazelnuts the explicitly accounted first-month staple; game remains supplemental.
Replace unsupported water pasteurisation, raw-organ meals and preserved-meat stock with observable boiling and same-day game consumption.
Retain a ceramic pot trial but remove it from the indispensable route. A wooden whorl provides the first spindle demonstration.
Separate successful construction from operational performance and community adoption.
Replace deterministic status displays with cautious, reciprocal first contact.
Track state through daily events and verify conservation automatically.
Expand the mission roadmap through measurement, surplus, institutions, industry and space systems.

Remaining limits
Reference notes have been edited for factual claims, dependency logic and practical scope. They remain drafts where detailed experimental verification or identification evidence is absent. The resource ledger is an internally consistent author model, not a demonstrated survival plan. Open setting decisions remain in Setting Specification.
The archive contains the removed prose and historical claims. Existing daily filenames are retained so external links do not silently break; displayed titles may describe the revised emphasis.
Completed revision and checks
The working vault now contains 145 Markdown notes: 28 daily entries, 99 capability notes, five era notes, and the setting, authoring and reference material. All 28 days and the pre-existing material, skill, tool and technology notes were revised. Unsupported claims were replaced with bounded methods or explicit research gaps; the archive preserves the earlier text.
The first month ends with an assembled but untested wooden thrower, green shaft candidates, a replacement spindle, a modest nut reserve and tentative reciprocal contact. Successful pottery, dependable fishing, large-game hunting and community-wide adoption are not claimed.
The default graph contains 141 prerequisite edges. Validation checks all wiki-links and linked headings, metadata and duplicate YAML keys, acyclic dependencies, demonstration order, asset and food quantities, fuel, and work-hour sums. In-memory defect checks confirm that it detects cyclic tool requirements, gifting the same spindle twice and reusing consumed rabbit meat. Archive integrity was checked against all 121 stored files, including the 118 original notes.
Generated acquisition views exclude undemonstrated pages and separate local observations from the traveller’s capability dates. Food disposition is explicit, so calorie estimates do not depend on prose wording. The export tools use only numbered content folders, sort days naturally, validate before writing and produce text parts outside the content graph.
These are editorial, structural and model-continuity checks. Dataview rendering has not been tested inside Obsidian, and the improvised techniques and assumed local resource yields have not been experimentally validated. No website was built or published in this revision.
Next substantive work
Develop reciprocal learning and seasonal preparation before asserting a stable specialist economy. Priorities are protection for feet and exposed skin, dependable shelter and water equipment, food yield and storage evidence, shared communication, and repeated independent production. Projectile trials are one bounded experiment within that work.
Later chapters should change scale to weeks, seasons and projects as appropriate. The expanded roadmap restores the original technical mission, with explicit route comparisons and acceptance tests through industrial production and spaceflight.
First six illustrations — 1 October 2026
The user approved the Day 1 watercolour-and-ink image and protagonist appearance. It is now the visual reference for subsequent Survival illustrations. The approved Day 1 image and five new scenes are embedded at the beginnings of Days 1–6. Illustration Continuity records the character, style, setting, event constraints and review workflow. Generated material-scale and tool-fitting errors in Days 5–6 were corrected before embedding. Image existence and metadata agreement are now included in the validator; visual accuracy remains an editorial check. The regional environmental frame is supported by R15, with the local resource assumptions retained as fiction.
Fresh illustrations for Days 7–10 — 2 October 2026
Following the user’s observation of artifacts in Days 5–6, the illustration workflow now generates each new scene independently from the original approved Day 1 reference. The brief favours smoother watercolour washes, selective ink and one clearly framed action. Defects prompt a new generation from Day 1 rather than successive edits of the defective output.
Four new illustrations are embedded at the beginnings of Days 7–10. They show the small awl test, hand-guided tool-case seam, rabbit panel preparation and modest carrying-cradle test, respectively. Days 8 and 9 were replaced by fresh generations after review of unnecessary or incorrectly scaled props. All selected outputs have zero edit passes. The daily prose is unchanged, and the PNG copies preserve the generated file bytes. Prompts, input paths, rejected attempts and selected outputs are recorded in _Artwork/survival/generation-prompts.json.
The vault validator and rebuilt context exports include the new embeds and metadata. Editorial visual inspection checks continuity; the images remain narrative illustrations rather than manufacturing drawings or verified archaeological reconstructions.
Tools illustration plates — 2 October 2026
All 19 Tools pages now open with an isolated manual-style illustration. The user requested the look of a mid-century illustrated blueprint; navy ink on ivory, concise part labels and selected detail views provide that treatment. After the first seven plates, the user asked for pastel colour in the remaining images. Those twelve plates add restrained natural-material washes.
Images follow the page-specific designs, including the wooden spindle whorl, failed clay specimen and continuous wooden spear point. Planned or untested designs retain their existing status. All tool-page prose is unchanged. Selected PNGs are stored in _Artwork/tools and embedded through relative paths above each page heading; illustration metadata records each scene and review date.
Fresh replacements clarified the knife-flake fracture face and removed a misplaced basket-base callout. The image service rejected several more detailed catalogue briefs for the hafted knife and spear plates; simpler non-procedural museum-style briefs succeeded. No selected output was created by repeated image edits. The gallery and generation manifest preserve the final outputs, briefs, earlier prompts and copy-integrity hashes.
Technology process illustrations — 2 October 2026
The user approved extending the manual illustration style to Technology pages, with compositions that explain processes, dependencies and testing. All 27 Technology pages now have opening plates with pastel washes, navy linework and concise captions. The set includes stage sequences, close-ups, cutaways and component studies. Existing page prose, resource events and demonstration status are unchanged.
The firing illustrations received fresh replacements to show stable dry supports independent of burning fuel. Pottery includes the cooled leak-test failure. Planned kiln and dart routes and the untested thrower retain explicit development labels. The rack illustration shows pelt drying without implying stored smoked meat.
The image service rejected several detailed carrier, dart and trap briefs. Simpler faithful studies succeeded. The final trap plates focus on candidate members and the running-loop component, leaving complete mechanism geometry and operating validation open. A generated assembled deadfall view was discarded for a misleading support relationship.
All selected PNGs are copied unchanged into _Artwork/technologies and embedded above page headings, with illustration metadata. The gallery collects all 27; the manifest records final and previous prompts, selected sources, references and copy hashes. Every selected output has zero edit passes. Editorial image inspection does not substitute for experimental verification of the processes.
Survival illustrations for Days 11–15 — 2 October 2026
Five new watercolour-and-ink opening scenes are embedded in Days 11–15. Each uses only the approved Day 1 reference for character and style. The set covers clay forming, inspection of the first usable needle eye, the unsuccessful riverside fishing trial, bedding replacement viewed from inside the shelter, and the separate firing trial as it burns down at dusk.
Camera positions vary while the shelter, uphill craft area, ordinary outside hearth and separate firing place retain their relative geography. The small fur pad appears only after fitting on Day 14, and the Day 15 pinch cup remains hot, in place and untested. Existing daily prose, asset events and capability status are unchanged.
Two needle close-ups were discarded for an oversized loose awl or an incorrect thread connection; the selected scene shows eye inspection before threading. A firing view with a constricted vessel neck and ambiguous support was replaced by a fresh scene specifying the same broad open pinch cup and its stone support. Several requests failed with network errors before producing images; these are recorded separately from visual rejections. No rejected output was used as a later reference.
Selected PNGs are copied unchanged into _Artwork/survival/day-11.png through day-15.png, with metadata above each page heading. The gallery, complete prompt manifest and five-day record preserve final briefs, earlier attempts, selected sources, copy hashes and the original daily-body hashes. All selected outputs have zero edit passes. Vault validation and context exports include these additions; editorial visual review does not establish experimental or archaeological validity.
Category specification and handbook migration — 2 October 2026
The user approved defining the four categories by the principal subject of each page: physical stock, practised ability, apparatus, and organised process or system. Category Specification now sets out the definitions, boundary cases, construction-page policy, development-state distinction, shared domains and authoring rules. Introduction, Style Guide and Page Templates use the same split and category-specific content expectations.
All 100 capability pages have one primary type/tag, a subtype and one or more topic domains. The current counts are 25 Materials, 26 Skills, 31 Tools and Equipment, and 18 Technologies — Processes and Systems. The existing type codes and stable IDs remain intact; historical ID prefixes do not determine current category.
Eleven object pages moved from technologies to equipment: the three bark/rawhide containers or carriers, two clothing pages, lean-to, drying rack, kiln, toolkit and two traps. Heating Stones moved from materials to equipment. Bifacial Knapping and Simple Hafting moved to skills; Nettle Retting moved to processes. Equipment is grouped by function in 05_Tools and Equipment. The wooden whorl and material alternatives are no longer filed according to an assumed construction material.
Process and skill titles were clarified: Camp Fire Management, Pit Firing, Coiled Basket Making, Edible Plant Identification and Medicinal Plant Assessment. Smoking Rack is now Drying Rack, reflecting its demonstrated pelt-processing role. Former names and paths remain aliases. The social skill and three systems previously in Mission now occupy their primary categories; Mission Coordination provides a reading route without duplicate capability pages. The dependency overview is now Capability Dependency Map, retaining its old name as an alias.
The new Bast Fibre material distinguishes prepared strip/fibre input from Bark Cordage output. Simple Cordage requires bast rather than finished cord; the output requires the fibre and twisting skill. Day 1 explicitly links the preparation it already described and records that input demonstration. No additional stock, food, fuel, work, capture or story outcome is created. The coiled-basket production route explicitly requires its existing coiling/weaving skill.
Topic Index groups related subjects across categories. Acquired and dependency views display the broader category names and subtypes. The validator now checks primary tags, subtypes, domains and category folders alongside links, image metadata, graph order and daily conservation. Normal view generation produces the topic index as its fourth view.
All approved PNGs stay in their original generation folders and retain their bytes. Original batch galleries and current equipment, skill and process galleries link to the migrated pages. Full prompts retain their historical wording; artwork records identify both original and current pages where moved. Workspace references follow the new paths.
The pre-migration snapshot is _RevisionArchive/2026-10-02-before-category-revision.zip. The approved specification, migration map and verification report record classifications, former paths and integrity checks. The verification checks preservation of existing IDs and demonstration dates, daily asset/food/fuel/water/work/sleep data, PNG hashes, former wiki-link targets, artwork references and ordinary Markdown links. New-policy defect checks exercise ambiguous primary types, wrong folders, invalid subtypes and missing domains. These are editorial and authored-consistency checks, not archaeological or experimental validation.
Survival illustrations for Days 16–20 — 2 October 2026
Five opening watercolour-and-ink scenes are embedded in Days 16–20: nettle-fibre extraction at the downstream rinsing place, light cord twisting, an upstream old-antler find, comparison of the rough biface, and the completed basket’s modest load test. Each uses only the approved original Day 1 image for character and style. Views vary with the action while the camp geography and limited clothing remain consistent.
The scenes keep the failed pot out of food use and distinguish objects acquired later in the day from the selected moment. Day 18 shows an old fragment away from a kill, Day 19 retains a rough unhafted tool, and Day 20’s basket scene precedes the cage work. The daily prose, resource events and demonstration status are unchanged.
Selected PNGs are copied unchanged into _Artwork/survival/day-16.png through day-20.png. The gallery, five-day briefs and complete prompt manifest retain selected sources, full prompts, fresh retries and any rejected outputs or service errors. All five selected images have zero edit passes. Original daily-body hashes and PNG copy hashes verify preservation. Vault validation and rebuilt context exports include the additions.
Survival illustrations for Days 21–28 — 2 October 2026
Eight opening watercolour-and-ink scenes complete the first month’s twenty-eight illustrated entries. They show wooden-whorl inspection, the small fish catch, pouch repair, the narrow fox shoulder panel, local cordage expertise, a shared spindle trial, green shafts under cover and grain inspection of the assembled thrower. Each uses only the approved Day 1 image for protagonist and style; no preceding or rejected image is passed forward.
The contact scenes show reciprocal practical attention outside the neighbours’ living area. Local participants already know cordage. The fox panel appears only from Day 24 and remains narrow; the first spindle is given away on Day 26 and replaced on Day 27. The shaft candidates and thrower retain their unfinished or untested status. The daily prose and resource events remain unchanged.
Selected PNGs are copied unchanged into _Artwork/survival/day-21.png through day-28.png. The eight-day gallery, briefs and full prompt manifest retain final prompts, sources, rejected outputs, retries and any interrupted requests. Source-copy hashes and original daily-body hashes verify preservation, as do the twenty preceding Survival PNG hashes. The pre-embedding snapshot is _RevisionArchive/2026-10-02-before-days-21-28-illustrations.zip. Vault validation and rebuilt context exports include the additions.
3 October 2026 — Earned contact, danger and intentions
This entry supersedes the earlier contact description above; those paragraphs record the previous edition, not current canon. The pre-edit source and four replaced PNGs are preserved in _RevisionArchive/2026-10-03-before-contact-revision.zip.

Days 4 and 6 now state the defensive purpose of the plain spear and the risk of animal scraps near bedding, within the existing work allowances. Their retained pictures still fit. Days 19–21 now connect distant smoke, evening firelight and cautious observation. Day 20 adds unidentified movement near camp; Day 22 adds a single wolf sighting, withdrawal and more deliberate spear access. Both are explicit fictional incidents, not evidence of local predator abundance.
Day 25’s cord and spindle pitch visibly fails to outperform local practice. A warning spear and nearby stone strike prompt retreat. The first spindle and samples are abandoned, not recorded as gifts; the resource events move the spindle loss to Day 25.
Day 26 becomes retreat, self-repair, defence and a reasoned choice of the atlatl. No fibre exchange or shared lesson occurs. Teaching and Knowledge Preservation returns to an undemonstrated planned capability. Days 27–28 state the intended useful comparison, projectile requirements and conditions for testing before any renewed visit.
Day 23 retains a limited 0.90 kg dressed fox lot for immediate cooking and consumption. Nut use falls to 0.32 kg; work increases by an hour and fuel by a kilogram. Damaged skin still becomes only the narrow Day 24 panel. Parasite risk is explicit; alleged whole-carcass contamination is removed.
Atlatl evidence is qualified: much later direct European finds make unfamiliarity plausible, not proven, and capable hand throwing prevents an automatic superiority claim. R16–R20 record the historical, anatomical, food-risk and knot sources used in this revision.
Days 22, 25 and 26 and the snare component receive fresh artwork. Original PNG bytes and prompt records are shelved. Retained scenes are checked against the revised day rather than regenerated unnecessarily. Day 25 replaces sapiens-like locals with anatomical Neanderthal features; Day 26’s former handling error is removed with its obsolete shared-lesson scene.

Generated views, current galleries and context exports are rebuilt from the authored sources. Validation checks consistency and file references; physical performance, food safety and exact anatomical reconstruction remain separate evidence limits.
3 October 2026 — User selection of the stone-pointed spear
Following the user’s preference and an evidence check, Day 25 restores the earlier stone-tipped illustration. That output was previously set aside for mismatch with the wooden-point wording, not because stone-tipped Neanderthal weapons were historically implausible. R21 records evidence supporting both types.
The text now identifies the local weapon as a knapped stone point fitted and bound into a wooden shaft. Day 26 recognises the locals’ composite-weapon expertise, while the traveller still owns his simpler wooden spear. Setting and illustration continuity distinguish ownership; observed equipment does not enter the traveller’s asset or demonstration ledger.
The restored rendering is copied byte-for-byte to day-25-v3-stone-point.png. The preceding wooden-point selection and complete selection record are shelved, and galleries and manifests follow the current choice. Historical prompts retain their actual wording, with the user’s approval of the stone-point variation recorded separately. The pre-change snapshot is _RevisionArchive/2026-10-03-before-stone-point-selection.zip.
3 October 2026 — Area map and Month 2 approval
The author approved the Month Two Outline and requested an illustrated area map before daily drafting. Valley Map adds a hand-drawn Day 28 overview and camp inset, with explicit compass choices, hydrology, landmark relationships, a same-bank contact route and provisional travel allowances. The written key governs decorative ambiguities. Resource patches are areas, predator sightings are not permanent landmarks, and no proposed Month 2 range, cache or shelter is represented as built.
World and Illustration Continuity now refer to that geography. The outline and roadmap record approval. First-month daily events, asset stocks and capability demonstrations are unchanged. The full map prompt, layout and selected-image receipt are retained under _Artwork/maps; the map starts with a fresh generation in built-in imagegen mode and receives one focused edit to correct the contact route and replace an invented raised table with a ground slab. The selected v2 rendering is copied without further image processing; source and copy hashes agree.
3 October 2026 — Days 29–35 and supporting text
The requested descending range 39–35 is interpreted as the approved opening week, Days 29–35. Seven text-only entries extend the second-person narrative with conservative trial outcomes, limited distant observation, cold-weather bedding work and the costs of reconnaissance. Ten new capability pages cover reference staff, practice dart and ground, plant insulation, willow strips, twining and pad, retreat judgement, throwing technique and food-reserve operation. Existing measurement, projectile-testing, dart-making and retting pages are extended; R22–R24 record the targeted evidence.
Daily events conserve the shaft-to-dart conversion, bindings, fibre, pad materials, fresh fish, food and fuel. No neighbour provisions or new images are added. Tools/update_views.py now preserves the original Days 1–28 ledger and creates a separate continuing Survival Ledger, avoiding a falsely labelled Day 28 inventory after later events. Navigation, geography additions and context exports follow the continuing state. The pre-change Markdown and tool snapshot is _RevisionArchive/2026-10-03-before-days-29-35.zip; the authoring specification is retained alongside it.
4 October 2026 — Design families, places and moon reflections
This update supersedes the four-category/structures-as-equipment convention in earlier historical entries. The handbook now has five capability subjects plus a separately typed local atlas within Structures and Places. Measurement and Records moves to Skills. The practice ground becomes a place; its former site-unit stock annotation is replaced by dated location preparation, while physical supplies and work budgets remain unchanged.
Atlatl absorbs its simple assembly route. Atlatl Dart absorbs Practice Dart and Dart Making, with practice, fletched and hunting variants on one page. Plant-Fibre Mats broadens the small bedding-pad subject; Split Wood Strips broadens the material subject with willow as the actual recorded route. Old names/path aliases and a merged-ID manifest preserve retrieval. Lean-to, drying framework and kiln enclosure move into Structures; the planned kiln is still unbuilt.
The new Reflections section contains full-moon Day 15 and new-moon Day 30 reviews restricted to those snapshots. Lunar Calendar defines a fictional arrival epoch and approximate fortnightly rhythm using the mean phase cycle, with upcoming reviews scheduled but unwritten. R25 records the astronomical context. Reflection tables are generated from cutoff ledger states, not the latest inventory; prose remains authored.
Validation, topic/dependency views, navigation, templates, artwork-gallery paths and exports follow the revised subjects. Approved PNGs and exact historical image prompts are preserved. The pre-change archive is _RevisionArchive/2026-10-04-before-structure-and-reflections.zip; _RevisionArchive/2026-10-04-page-migration.json records current targets.
4 October 2026 — reading order, lunar day labels and artwork
Moved Reflections to 02 and Structures and Places to 06, with other sections renumbered into reader order. Survival filenames, titles and links now use Moon N Day M; continuous day IDs and the physical ledger remain intact. Old day/folder names are retained as aliases. The calendar uses rounded mean new-moon boundaries, so Moon 2 starts on continuous Day 30. Added an end-of-Day-1 arrival reflection and numbered the three reviews in reading order, with snapshot validation.
Generated and embedded seven Survival illustrations for Days 29–35 and twelve missing tool, technology and place plates using the built-in image tool. Nineteen selected outputs have zero edit passes and verified identical source/copy hashes; nine rejected renderings and their prompts are recorded separately. Previous illustrations are unchanged. Reflection art remains at the proposal stage; its three compositions and style alternatives are in Reflection Artwork Proposals.
Recovery/provenance: _RevisionArchive/2026-10-04-before-moons-and-art.zip, the day/section migration map, and _Artwork/2026-10-04/generation-prompts.json. Physical stock, food, fuel, water, work/sleep, ongoing processes and location records were compared against the pre-change snapshot and preserved for all 35 days.
4 October 2026 — approved reflection artwork
Added the three approved watercolour/gouache/graphite chapter frontispieces to the arrival, first-full-moon and next-new-moon Reflection pages. Images were generated afresh with the built-in image tool from the original identity reference, with explicitly limited cup/launcher geometry references. Each PNG was copied unchanged into _Artwork/reflections, prompts and selection provenance were recorded, and reflection prose and cutoff ledgers were preserved. The index and current illustration guidance now record the selected series.
4 October 2026 — Reflection 03 anatomy correction
Replaced the apparent three-leg pose with a freshly generated seated composition showing two distinct legs and feet. Saved the selected PNG unchanged as reflection-03-new-moon-v2.png, shelved the former selection, and updated the page, gallery and generation provenance. Reflection prose, cutoff inventory and the other two frontispieces are unchanged. The pre-correction records are archived in 2026-10-04-before-reflection-03-anatomy.zip.
5 October 2026 — Moon 2 Days 7–11
Added continuous Days 36–40 in second-person present tense, following the approved “curiosity without admiration” phase. The Day 37 atlatl comparison preserves the local adult’s practiced superiority, and the Day 39 access warning has a real gathering cost. All acquisitions come from the traveller’s own work. Fish-closure repair, a rabbit catch and unfinished pelt, small textile sample and limited grass back panel develop existing lines without supplying instant winter clothing or a hunting weapon.
Added a Spear Throwing skill page for the separately observed local practice and one broad equipment-family page, Plant-Fibre Clothing, with actual construction, allocation, fit checks, upkeep and evidence limits. Extended the existing fish-trap, deadfall, projectile, pelt, twining, material and process pages instead of making separate articles for each repair or sample. The area atlas and illustration guidance retain dated state, with no new artwork. The month-two outline records progress, remaining Days 41–42 priorities and the unchanged later hunting/observer arcs.
Ledger events account for food, grass, yarn, line, withes, pelt, ordinary fuel/water and active labour. The Day 35 body previously said 8.5 hours while its unchanged work budget totalled nine; that prose figure is corrected. Existing daily events and reflection cutoffs remain intact. Recovery snapshot: _RevisionArchive/2026-10-05-before-days-36-40.zip. The authoring script and continuity comparison are retained alongside it.
5 October 2026 — Moon 2 Days 12–16 and full-moon review
Added continuous Days 41–45 and Reflection 04 at the completed Day 44 cutoff. The shelter audit drives staged construction without dismantling the old occupied roof. Food, fuel, acorn charges, accepted fibre, short line, structural pieces, mixed cover and clean bedding have separate allocations. All acquisitions remain independent. No hunt, large pelt, winter performance, ceramic firing, supplied refuge or neighbour benefit is invented.
Added the broad Shelter Construction skill, Framed Debris Shelter family and Plant Covering Stock material; extended existing fibre, food, bedding and atlas pages. R33 records the limited acorn-processing analogy. Updated the remaining month-two priorities and roadmap. Recovery snapshot: _RevisionArchive/2026-10-05-before-days-41-45.zip. New artwork is commissioned against the finalized daily and cutoff states, with original identity/style references and independent renders.
5 October 2026 — Moon 2 Days 17–21
Added continuous Days 46–50 with independently earned food, yarn, cord, cover, bedding and clothing allocations. The first shower exposes a repairable leak; a canid investigation costs craft time; a short deer approach ends without a cast and reduces gathering. The front panel expands the existing plant-clothing family, and one existing rabbit pelt becomes one limited crown covering. Day 50’s private casts do not pre-empt the later observer arc.
Added the reusable Hunting Approach judgement page and extended existing family/process/atlas pages. R34 records limited modern attractant-management reasoning and R35 red-deer vigilance evidence, separating them from authored events and yields. Recovery snapshot: _RevisionArchive/2026-10-05-before-days-46-50.zip. Earlier daily pages and four reflection cutoffs are preserved. Illustration completion and unchanged PNG source-copy provenance are recorded in _Artwork/2026-10-05-days-46-50/generation-prompts.json.
7 October 2026 — Days 51–55 and narrative course correction
Added five consecutive daily pages, Moon 2 Days 22–26, following the author’s direction to reduce routine/resource narration and restore the technology-handbook purpose. Each page centres a practical mechanism, its test and what it enables. Modest supply estimates remain behind the prose for conservation; no new routine crisis or convenient large-game kill drives the sequence.
Added Wooden Mallet, Wooden Splitting Wedge and Plant-Fibre Footwear reference families, and extended existing weaving, ignition, vessel and projectile notes. Recorded second-kit and second-vessel construction independently; footwear remains experimental and atlatl interest remains short of adoption. No earlier day or reflection cutoff is rewritten. Style Guide and Page Templates now preserve this direction for future writing. Pre-edit Markdown snapshot: _RevisionArchive/2026-10-07-before-days-51-55.zip.
R36 and R37 record limited later analogies for wooden splitting tools and layered footwear. Their performance and dates are not transferred to the fictional valley. Daily artwork and prompts are recorded separately in the new generation batch.
9 October 2026 — Dated protagonist character sheet
Created Character Sheet - Moon 2 Day 23 at the completed Day 52 clothing cutoff, following the user’s report of a rabbit-head hat and disappearing garments. Three full-body views retain the same protagonist, plain shallow fur crown pad, anatomical-left fox strip, separate front/back grass screens, bark waist layers with small pelvic pad, and both experimental bast soles. Detail studies clarify crown construction, sole/liner and waist layers.
The built-in image-generation tool used the original approved Day 1 image for identity/style and the Plant-Fibre Clothing equipment plate for construction only. The defective Day 52 rendering was not used as an input. Exact prompt, input roles, review and matching source-copy hashes are saved in _Artwork/character-sheets/moon-2-day-23/generation-prompts.json. Illustration Continuity and Style Guide now require the dated clothing sheet alongside the original identity reference, with explicit reasons and locations for removed clothing. The earlier animal-head defect is recorded as a missed visual check.
No daily narrative, inventory event, reflection cutoff or garment-performance claim changes. Guidance recovery snapshot: _RevisionArchive/2026-10-09-before-character-sheet.zip.
9 October 2026 — Regenerate Moon 2 Days 23–26
Replaced continuous Days 52–55 with independent built-in image-generation outputs using the approved Day 1 identity/style and new dated clothing sheet. Day 52 shows the short level walking trial with both bast soles; Day 53 shows the kit’s packing stage after the extinguished ignition trial; Day 54 shows cold containment inspection. All three wear the complete dry-use outfit. Day 55 preserves the written casting removals and depicts exactly two grass screens, the crown pad and both soles protected nearby, with a blunt unfletched dart and short integral-hook thrower.
Visual review rejected one reversed-shoulder Day 53 render and two Day 55 renders for object geometry or an apparent third grass panel. 09_reference/survival-ledger.title: Survival Ledger
09_reference/survival-ledger.content:
Survival Ledger
Qualitative continuity
Narrative continues through Day 114. Exact resource accounting ends at Day 59; historical totals below are not the current inventory. Later entries record only consequential changes. Routine meals, fuel, water and hour balances are not required. Read the narrative for material plausibility, current supply and unfinished work.
Day 60

Western Overhang inspected as the new home site; no construction or move yet.

Day 61

Western Overhang becomes the occupied home; the old camp is abandoned rather than maintained as a retreat.
Movable working equipment and usable supplies are transferred; the old dirty drying frame and rejected pot stay behind. The riverside fish cage stays at its anchor.
Basic bed and first windward brush/bark screen are in use; no mud panel or full front closure yet.

Day 62

A familiar local adult accepts branchwood carrying and a small splitting contribution; one worn previously worked deer-sized fur-on skin is visibly transferred in return.
The new skin is protected at Western Overhang, not worn or cut into a garment yet; no food, weapon or blanket access is included in the exchange.

Day 63

The acquired worked skin becomes one overlapping thigh-length wrap: hair inward, tan skin outside, upper-edge fold, repaired left shoulder and a chest tie with a light waist fastening.
Both grass torso screens are set aside dry. Bark waist layers and pelvic pad remain underneath; the narrow fox strip is retained under the left shoulder. Plain crown pad and both bast soles remain worn.
No new hood, leg garment, hide shoes or separate large blanket is made from the same skin.

Day 64

A low food-only rack and clean bark spreading surfaces are installed in the dry rear-right recess; the existing basket gains a loose woven cover.
Own gathering adds a modest inspectable nut batch. Untreated acorns remain processing stock; cooked wet meal is used promptly and is not counted as winter stores.

Day 65

The front screen gains a short return and a movable entrance baffle; the dog-leg southeast opening and high ventilation gap remain clear.
Compressed bedding is renewed locally. A brief shower leaves the sleeping strip dry; the hearth remains outside.

Day 66

One small lower woven bay receives a fresh earth/grass infill charge under roof protection; two witness patches are left to dry.
No full mud wall, coated roof or completed drying result is claimed. Pottery stock and fired comparison pieces are kept separate.

Day 67

The existing fox shoulder panel from the traveller’s Day 23 snare catch is removed from beneath the body wrap and reallocated entirely to the rabbit cap’s side/ear/nape extension; no new pelt or exchange occurs.
The body wrap is refitted at shoulder and waist without cutting armholes. The bark waist layers, pelvic pad and original two bast soles remain; the left shoulder no longer carries a separate fox panel.

Day 68

A controlled shallow-margin session with the original integral wooden-point spear catches one small fish, cooked and eaten the same day.
The fish cage stays at its existing anchor. No multi-pronged tool, stone hunting joint or preserved fish supply is made.

Day 69

One separate sound fallen-oak shaft is selected and dressed; a fresh gravel blank becomes a stout bifacial stone spear point. Parts remain unhafted and no impact or hunting result occurs.
The earth trial has a firm-centred witness patch after several mild intervals; its small installed bay retains its keys with fine edge shrinkage. No whole-front daub programme is completed.

Day 70

The Day 69 stone point is seated and mechanically bound into its separate oak shaft with new nettle cord. Light hand-load checks show no visible movement; no impact or hunting result occurs yet.
One existing deadfall catches a rabbit. Its meat is cooked and consumed the same day; one new pelt is promptly fleshed and placed on a small removable dirty-work support for protected drying/working.

Day 71

A newly selected clean food-only slab and handstone reduce scattering and uneven acorn particles; a modest charge is leached, cooked and eaten, leaving the rest of the nuts dry.
A second existing deadfall catches a rabbit. Its meat is consumed that day; its distinct pelt is fleshed and joins the Day 70 pelt in protected drying/working. Both skins remain material, not footwear yet.

Day 72

One fresh modest same-source clay charge becomes an open pinch-form greenware pot with a comparable witness piece, on a separate protected craft-side drying board. It is unfired, unfilled and unavailable for cooking.
The two fired comparison remnants remain intact and separate from the new charge and wall mixture. Both newly caught pelts continue protected drying and mechanical working.

Day 73

The distinct Day 70 and Day 71 rabbit skins are allocated one per foot to low hair-in removable coverings, pale skin outward, enclosing toes/heels to just above ankles. No loose pelt stock or legging material remains from those catches.
Both original bast soles remain outside/beneath as the wearing layer. Dry grass lining, retained ties and short new cord extensions complete a limited dry-camp fit trial; no waterproofing, durable tanning or long-walk result is established.

Day 74

A controlled slow push and short restrained thrusts into a loose plant target give the composite spear its first limited impact/load result. The seat remains aligned; a settled outer binding turn is taken up. No animal, cast, hunt or injury is involved.
Low pelt foot coverings receive a short dry-camp repeat use and lining inspection. The new pot remains greenware; its witness centre is still yielding, so no firing or water use occurs before the full-moon review.

Day 75

New short bark-cord heel keepers lead retention through the original bast-sole edge bindings, reducing pull on thin pelt folds. No new skin or footwear pair is acquired.
A short dry near-camp working outing retains the layers after adjustment; wet-weather durability and lower-leg coverage remain unresolved.

Day 76

Original dart A gains two modest bound feather vanes from the retained Day 27 lot and an integral wooden point. It is the same projectile, without stone point, separate foreshaft, adhesive or second completed dart.
The rear engagement stays clear; slow fit and modest initial launch checks reveal no snag or immediate vane movement. Bowed blank B remains unfinished.

Day 77

At the re-inspected west-facing practice ground, the modified original dart and the separate stone-pointed spear receive limited casts. No point, binding or vane shifts visibly; differing equipment and technique prevent a controlled performance claim.
A familiar adult at the outer working edge allows a short accompanying movement after indicating the western route. No food, skin, weapon, general access right or standing invitation transfers.

Day 78

The traveller accompanies three local hunters with explicit scene-level permission, but makes no cast; local hunters take one red deer. He helps hold, separate and carry after the kill.
A small observed meat-and-fat share is cooked and consumed that day. One trimmed narrow fresh hide margin is visibly released to him, promptly fleshed and put on the dirty-work support; it is not worn or duplicated into other stock.
No whole hide, personal atlatl kill, standing alliance, preserved meat or general access right is gained.

Day 79

A separate sound willow section becomes a compact four-pronged wooden fishing spear with spacers and new binding. The original single-point wooden spear, stone-pointed hand spear and modified dart remain separate.
After a non-living shallow-water contact check, one small fish is caught, cooked and eaten the same day. No stored fish or dependable yield is inferred.
The Day 78 hide margin continues protected drying with a damp fold opened; no garment allocation or tanning result occurs. The pot remains unfired pending a deliberate readiness inspection.

Day 80

The entire retained narrow Day 78 deer-hide margin is shaped into one small edge-cover blank around a wooden former, using bark cord; local dampening permits folding and protected drying continues. It is not clothing, leather or a second skin lot.
The new cover remains unfinished until its dry fit on Day 81; the Day 72 pot stays unfired.

Day 81

The same Day 78 deer margin finishes drying around the former; one Stone-Edge Guard passes a gentle dry fit/removal trial for an existing flake and enters light-tool storage. No wardrobe change.
The Day 72 witness is broken into two halves: one raw control is retained and the other accompanies the still-unfired pot. Dry-looking fresh section and base/rim inspection justify cautious preheating, not a measured moisture result.
The already identified northeast firing patch is cleared and fuel staged; no firing or new kiln occurs today.

Day 82

One Day 72 pot and one half of its witness receive a gradual open firing on the existing northeast patch and remain untouched to cool overnight. The other witness half stays unfired; the earlier comparison remnants are not re-fired.
No hot handling, quenching, kiln, containment test or food use occurs. The ordinary outdoor hearth and bark cooking route remain separate and active.

Day 83

The cold Day 72 vessel is recovered intact. Its fired witness half stays coherent under a separate wetting check; the raw half softens and is discarded at the non-food test spot.
The pot holds two increasing cold-water charges during a limited check, with initial dampening but no crack, softening or steady drip. One useful ceramic vessel is first demonstrated; waterproofness, production repeatability and cooking performance are not yet established.
The vessel airs under cover after test water is discarded. It has not yet been heated in use or used for food.

Day 84

Three dry selected support stones form a low stable pot support at the existing outdoor ordinary hearth; this is not the ceramic firing patch or an indoor hearth.
The one Day 72 pot completes a gradual water-only heating/cooling cycle, is inspected cold, then cooks a fresh separately leached acorn charge on a second gradual cycle. No hot-stone insertion, quenching, glaze, handles or lid.
The entire meal is eaten the same day; the vessel is washed and air-dried. Two observed use cycles are a useful limited result, not a production-reliability or chemical food-contact certification. The guard, clothing and existing weapons retain their states.

Day 85

One newly cut sound green hazel stem is split; one selected half becomes the sole bow stave. The other half remains ordinary working stock, not a second accepted stave.
Two low clean forked rests support the green stave at the craft side, separate from the food rack and dirty pelt frame. No bending, stringing, shooting or fixed seasoning deadline.

Day 86

A short newly prepared nettle trial line with a remade overlap and sample eye receives gentle static pull checks against a separate bark sample. No full bowstring, rated strength or dynamic acceptance is established.
Three new green hazel shoots are selected and trimmed as separate arrow-shaft blanks on the clean support. No heads, nocks, fletching, completed arrows or conversion of dart B.

Day 87

The same green hazel half-stave is coarsely shaped on its split/belly face, retaining the continuous back and generous working allowance. No nocks, stringing, loaded tillering or shooting.
Tillering is explained as a future judgement task, not entered as a demonstrated skill. Three arrow blanks and the short trial line remain unfinished.

Day 88

A local shrinkage-edge draught in the existing small daub bay is diagnosed against sound backing and steady supports, then repaired with a small fresh building mix under the retained bark cover. No full mud wall, new roof or indoor hearth.
The repair begins protected drying. Clothing remains the Day 73 outfit with exposed lower legs; no hide stock, garment or hunting success is added. Bow work remains unstrung and green.

Day 89

Boundary entry required by the existing Day 89 new-moon milestone. The same single pot completes another gradual meal-use cycle and remains sound after cooling; the fresh meal is consumed that day.
Overnight rain leaves the bed and craft-side wood inside the dry strip. The Day 88 edge repair remains drying; no new material, accepted bowstring, working bow, arrow, hide, alliance or completed winter supply appears.

Day 90

One existing deadfall is relocated a short distance on the established western circuit, with a firm base, a remote release check and a small bark drip cover. No new deadfall, cage, fish device or catch is added.
Red deer are observed on familiar west-bank ground without a new mapped route, site, river crossing or contact. The traveller chooses independent winter work. Clothing and green bow stock remain unchanged.

Day 91

One new nettle trap-line candidate and separate short test offcuts are prepared from retained fibre. Wet movement, attachment creep and contact chafing are compared under modest non-animal loads. The original short bowstring sample is not consumed.
The new snare arrangement remains a bench trial, not an operating field trap or a catch. Existing atlatl/dart A and stone-pointed spear are inspected; no new weapon, head, vane, hide or clothing change.

Day 92

One new simple frame has two light rails, two crosspieces, plant bindings, a diagonal line brace, broad plaited bast shoulder bands, bark/grass bearing pads and separate load ties. Modest wrapped-stone walking checks are not a rated load or conversion of the small hide sling.
A further observation of already known deer informs one chosen open casting position on familiar western ground. No shot, catch, new named hunting place, group help or ready bow.

Day 93

First personally taken large game: one smaller antlerless red deer, secured solo with the existing pointed wooden dart A from the atlatl. No neighbour, shared kill, loan, new stone dart head or bow. Dart A is recovered with tip damage; shaft, two vanes and rear seat remain.
The one whole main skin is promptly cleaned in the field and again at the overhang; it has a small dart opening and uneven edges. No garment, tanned leather or additional skin lot is manufactured by the kill.
Two manageable pack-frame trips retain the single skin and limited selected fresh food for prompt use. Remaining carcass material is left unrecovered and not counted as a future cache. A small actual food-fat portion is cooked with the meal; no dressing-fat reserve or preserved meat stock is granted.
Cold, dry frosty weather and separate airy bark-covered supports allow a short holding interval for the remaining selected cuts. This authored temporary holding is not measured refrigeration, freezing, validated storage or a winter reserve. The full skin stays open at the separate dirty-work side.

Day 94

One new smoothed wooden fleshing beam is held by a stable low fork/rest and ground stop at the dirty-work area. A larger open hide-support instance is made separately from the little rabbit support, food rest and clean bow rests.
The same Day 93 full skin receives supported tissue removal and light open margin support. It remains an unfinished hair-bearing skin, not tanned leather, ready sleeves, leggings, boots or a new character-sheet state. No body/leg panels are cut or allocated yet.
The limited food held from Day 93 is cooked and used promptly across Day 94; none remains as an authorised fresh-meat reserve at this cutoff. No drying, smoking, freezing, preserved fat or shelf-stable ration is demonstrated.
Dart A alone has its damaged integral wooden tip reshaped after cleaning; no new head, shaft or vane is added. It needs another trial before reuse. Current clothing and unstrung green bow stock remain unchanged, with no community work.

Day 95

The sole full Day 93 red-deer skin completes an authored staged drying/scraping/flexing trial. Useful body areas bend for layout by evening; thicker ragged margins are excluded from planned garment areas. No new skin or cutting yet.
Mechanical hair-retaining preparation uses no added oil, brain dressing, salt, alum or smoke. It is worked untanned skin, not chemically or oil-tanned leather, and will need dry storage and repeated care. The analogy is caribou practice, not a validated red-deer schedule.
Existing full cap, sleeveless tan wrap and low enclosing foot covers remain unchanged. Earlier selected deer food was used by Day 94; background meals use remaining autumn stores, with no new nut harvest or food reserve.

Day 96

The one worked skin is cut once into two sleeve panels, two leg-wrap panels, small folded reinforcing tabs and limited seam-test scraps. The small dart opening and ragged/thick margins are avoided. No whole uncut hide, new footwear, mitten or blanket reserve remains.
New fine plant sewing thread and fastening lengths come from retained prepared nettle/bast stock. No deer tendon, new sinew, dressing fat or carcass retrieval is assumed. The old bone needle and awl are reused.
Sleeve seams and leg-panel margins are in progress. The new limb outfit is not worn yet; the Day 73 character sheet still governs the selected cutting scene and overnight wardrobe. Garment fit and attachments complete on Day 97.

Day 97

Two removable hair-in red-deer sleeves and two overlapping above-knee-to-ankle leg panels are fitted and worn by Day 97. Leg tops extend beneath the existing above-knee wrap hem. Sleeve tabs attach to sound shoulder edges, clear of the anatomical-left repair; loose leg keepers rise to the existing waist line.
One skin supplies only this four-panel set plus small tabs/test scraps. The original tan body wrap, full grey-brown crown with tan fox ear/nape sides, and BOTH low closed pale rabbit foot covers over visible bast soles remain. Hands remain bare. No hood, new boots, cloak, trousers or reserve hide.
Character Sheet - Moon 4 Day 9 fixes appearance after this completed fit, superseding the Day 73 sheet for subsequent scenes only. Dampness, re-stiffening and maintenance remain unresolved performance questions rather than a waterproof claim.
Short local trap inspection yields no catch. The solitary winter continues without exchange, group labour or resource ledgers. Dart A awaits its post-reshaping trial; the bow stock remains unstrung.

Day 98

New modest netting cord is made from retained prepared fibre, independently of the original bowstring sample and Day 91 snare candidate. One smoothed wooden mesh gauge and one small hand-knotted rectangular panel are made; the panel is folded/side-joined into a shallow open-mouth bag.
One flexible willow frame rod is selected but no completed hand net exists at the Day 98 cutoff. The wet panel trial leads to remaking one slipping join; this is not rated mesh or a catch. The existing woven trap is inspected empty, cap reseated and reset in its familiar near-bank placement.
The complete Day 97 sleeve/leg outfit is worn; cap, original tan wrap and both low pale foot covers persist. No new shared material, warm-weather harvest, fish, second vessel or completed bow.

Day 99

One shallow-bag hand net is completed from the Day 98 mesh, selected willow oval, short wooden handle and new lacing/binding stock. Wet non-animal loading precedes use. Its modest single-use result supplies no load rating, large fish capability, set net, seine or weir.
One small fish from the existing near-bank woven trap is transferred through its rear cap into the hand net, promptly dispatched, cooked and consumed that day. No preserved ration or further animal skin is introduced. Retrieval cap is reseated and the old trap remains in service.
New arm/leg coverings remain in use with old full cap, tan wrap and both low closed foot covers over bast soles. Hand net is rinsed, inspected and hung draining away from dirty hide work. No group help, new shelter, bow use or website update.

Day 100

One small wooden fishing gorge with a centre attachment, one separate modest new nettle hand line and a smooth stick winder are made. A loose wet-bark fold supplies an inert turning comparison; no fish, curved hook, rod, reel, metal or set line is introduced.
New hand-line stock is separate from the Day 91 snare candidate, Day 86 bowstring sample and the existing net. A little more retained retted material is cleaned for later dry fibre work; no new winter nettle harvest or numerical stock reset.
A brief restrained target trial checks reshaped dart A after Day 94. Its same wooden point, shaft, rear seat and two vanes remain sound; it is available again without a new kill, head or spare dart. Bowed dart B is still unfinished.
The completed Day 97 outfit remains: full cap, original tan wrap, sleeves/leg panels, both low closed foot covers and bast soles. No garment or hide acquisition.

Day 101

A few actual earthworms are found in unfrozen sheltered leaf mould during a mild damp interval and used as bait. This is a local authored observation, not guaranteed winter availability, a new human food or an identified modern species.
The Day 100 hand line/gorge receives a small separately tied smooth stone sinker. One modest fish is taken from an accessible quiet near-bank pocket, landed with the existing hand net, promptly dispatched, cooked and consumed on Day 101. No stored fish, new trap, rod, reel, main-river crossing or abundant run.
Light rain dampens a sleeve cuff; gentle drying and flexing follow at the overhang. The existing complete outfit remains, with no new dressing fat, waterproofing or new footwear. All line is retrieved and aired, not left fishing unattended.

Day 102

The existing Day 27 replacement wooden spindle is reused, not reinvented or replaced. Previously retained retted material cleaned on Day 100 is now dry and supplies two newly spun modest singles, then one small separate two-ply yarn lot.
Spindle rotation during plying opposes the singles twist. Small release/feed adjustments and one separate wet sample support a limited handling trial, not a breaking-strength gain, industrial productivity claim or bowstring acceptance. The remaining dry yarn is reserved for the Day 103 netting work.
No first-month yarn is reclaimed from stored clothing or old twining. No wool, flax harvest, new fibre field, workshop structure or loom appears. The coarse retained nettle remainder diminishes; the bow, trial bowstring sample, snare candidate and hand line remain separate.

Day 103

One slim double-end-notched wooden netting shuttle is made from retained split stock and smoothed after a snagging corner is found. It carries the new Day 102 plied yarn; the existing separate plain gauge still sets loop size.
A modest separate rectangular repair-sized mesh panel is completed and retained with the intact hand net. It is not a second hand net, enlarged net, cage, seine or operational set net. No old yarn is recovered from garments.
The Day 103 full-moon reflection closes after this completed day. No Day 104 string, bow draw, new catch, skin, exchange or cooperation is known at its cutoff. The complete Day 97 outfit remains, with sleeves loosened/hung nearby only at the evening review.

Day 104

One new full-length nettle bowstring candidate is manufactured from its own selected prepared fibre, with one worked-back eye and a long free end for later adjustment. Only modest static handling is recorded; no fitted attachment, dynamic acceptance, strength rating or shooting capability. The short Day 86 sample remains separate.
Bowstring demonstration records this first full-length candidate manufacture, not an accepted bow/string system. The green rough hazel stave is inspected without new cracks observed, then returned unstrung. No loaded tillering, draw, arrow completion or bow shot occurs.
Day 102 yarn/Day 103 repair mesh are not consumed for the heavier string. Separate snare candidate and fishing line remain. Existing full clothing and one pot persist; no hide, dressing fat, wool, new winter fibre harvest or group help.
A light patchy snow dusting appears outside on Day 104; the sheltered craft surface and selected fibre remain dry. This is authored December weather, not a reconstructed temperature or a guarantee of freezing food storage.

Day 105

One adult rabbit is taken in the existing Day 90 relocated deadfall, inspected/reset, and retained food is freshly cooked/consumed on Day 105. This occasional authored catch does not establish abundant rabbits or a winter yield.
One new sound main rabbit skin is promptly fleshed and opened on the existing small dirty-side support. It is separate from the cap/foot pelts and the wholly allocated Day 93 deer hide. No mittens are cut or worn yet; no fat or sinew reserve is credited.
Lower snow patches are melting, shaded remnants persist. All existing clothes remain; the rough bow remains unstrung and three arrow blanks unfinished at cutoff.

Day 106

First actual low-deflection floor-tillering comparison on the single Day 85/87 hazel body. Small belly-only removals adjust a stiff area; the continuous back is preserved. No string is fitted, no arrow made or shot.
Surface feel and shaving behaviour inform a cautious authored trial, not proof of full seasoning. No moisture reading, drying deadline, draw weight or hunting rating is claimed. The body rests unloaded between checks.
The Day 105 rabbit skin receives staged protected drying and mechanical working; useful margins begin folding. It remains one uncut skin, no new clothes or dressing treatment.

Day 107

One same hazel body gains smooth side string seats, a fitted Day 104 string eye and an adjustable terminal hitch. Short restrained pulls and belly adjustments lead to a low-braced experimental practice bow. This is first assembled-bow demonstration, not a fully seasoned or hunting-rated weapon. No dry release or shot.
One of three Day 86 arrow blanks becomes a plain unfletched practice arrow with integral rounded wooden nose, self-nock and a short new fine plant-thread reinforcing wrap. Two original blanks remain unfinished. No stone/metal head, feathers, new shaft lot or extra dart.
The Day 105 rabbit skin finishes protected working/rest before layout, still uncut. Existing clothes remain unchanged. The bow is unstrung and inspected at the end of work.

Day 108

The single Day 105 adult-rabbit skin is allocated after working and actual hand layout to TWO small thumb-less closed hand pockets, folded/sewn with hair inward, short wrist openings and loose retainers, plus minor seam-test scraps. No separate thumb stalls, long gauntlets, shoe repairs or spare whole pelt.
The new covers warm resting/loosely closed hands; they are removed for fine work and archery. They are an authored simple mitten-family variant, not a copied Arctic pattern or a waterproof/durable-leather claim. New fine nettle thread, existing awl and old bone needle are used; no new sinew or fat reserve.
Character Sheet - Moon 4 Day 20 fixes appearance after fitting: all existing cap/wrap/sleeves/leg panels and both low closed foot covers remain, with the two optional removable pale hand pockets. No torso, leg, head or foot garment is replaced.

Day 109

First short controlled bow releases at the existing Projectile Practice Ground, using the same low-braced experimental hazel bow and ONE rounded-nose unfletched practice arrow. The same arrow is retrieved/inspected each time. Untidy short flight and intact recovered equipment are authored observations; no hunting range, accuracy, draw weight or fully seasoned state is certified.
Both new hand covers are deliberately removed together onto clean dry bark for shooting, then worn again for return. A light temporary sleeve retainer gives string clearance; no new permanent garment, archery glove or extra hide. All other current clothing and low footwear stay in service.
The bow is unstrung after the limited session; first fitted natural string remains inspectable, no dry fire, animal shot, new game, surplus, fletching or head. Two original arrow blanks and bowed dart B remain unfinished. Next reflection remains Day 118.

Day 110

Two newly found sound loose flight feathers from an unidentified bird supply two modest matched vane sections for the existing Day 107 arrow. This is a distinct new lot; original Day 27 feathers and dart A remain unchanged. No bird catch, meat, surplus feathers or new arrow is credited.
Fresh fine plant thread binds the two opposing vane strips without a new adhesive or sinew allocation. Nock, release-finger and bow-hand clearance are checked by handling; no shot is made on Day 110.
All current clothing remains. Both hand pockets are removed together for fine work. One provisional bow remains unstrung; two original arrow blanks and dart B remain unfinished.

Day 111

One small fish is caught with the existing Day 79 four-pronged willow fishing spear from dry stable bank footing. It is promptly dispatched, separately dressed, freshly cooked and wholly used on Day 111. No species, winter run, regular catch rate or preserved stock is inferred.
Minor tip roughness is scraped; lower binding/spacers remain serviceable. The ordinary wooden spear, stone-pointed hand spear, dart A and bow are not substituted or dismantled.
There is still one useful pot. Its food/water scheduling bottleneck motivates a second vessel, not an instant duplicate, a second hearth, a quantified fuel saving or simultaneous unsupported heating. Bark/hot-rock equipment remains the fallback.

Day 112

A fresh modest local clay charge supplies ONE new plain open cooking bowl and ONE comparable same-body drying witness. The bowl is somewhat wider than the existing pot, without handles, spout or foot ring. No new temper recipe, volume measurement or firing is claimed.
Both new pieces are unfired greenware at the separate protected craft board. The old Day 72/82 pot is the sole working vessel; earlier fired/remnant samples are not consumed or reassigned.
New material stays away from raw-skin work, food surfaces, excluded wet corner and direct hearth heat. Existing roof/screen and outside hearth remain unchanged.

Day 113

One newly selected sound fresh willow section supplies one shallow one-piece wooden spoon with substantial neck, simple handle and smooth rim. No adze, metal gouge, fire hollowing, oil/fat finish, extra bowl or food allocation is invented. Existing stirring stick remains a different implement.
The spoon receives a first limited meal-use trial in the OLD working pot with already stored/processed food used that day. Rinsing, raised-fibre rework and airy drying are described; no generic unknown wood is declared food-safe.
The Day 112 bowl and sole witness remain unfired; yielding underside means no firing acceptance. Current clothes remain, with both hand pockets removed together for carving and food handling.

Day 114

Same Day 107 arrow with Day 110 two-vane addition receives a few short controlled trials at the existing practice ground. The same arrow is retrieved each time; no new shaft, head, hunt or range/accuracy measurement. Reduced visible yaw is an authored observation confounded by release/air conditions, not a controlled proof.
Both hand pockets are removed together for bow work; a temporary sleeve keeper is reused as a type, not a new permanent garment. Bow/string remain provisional, inspected and stored unstrung. Two original shaft blanks and dart B remain unfinished.
Day 112 greenware bowl/witness remain unfired at cutoff. Bowl is moved only once supported firmness allows; witness still yields. One old pot remains the sole working vessel; spoon stays in use. No pot firing, preserved food, group aid or reflection. Next reflection Day 118.

Historical quantitative record through Day 59
Scope and assumptions
This is a generated author continuity model, not measured survival performance. Daily frontmatter is the source of truth. Regenerate with python tools/update_views.py after editing events, then run python tools/validate_vault.py. The original prose is preserved in the pre-revision archive.
The fictional valley has productive hazel patches within a manageable daily circuit in early autumn. Kernel weights are edible mass after shelling; shells are excluded. Gathering and processing take daily labour. Recorded collection is a setting assumption requiring palaeoecological and field review, not a demonstrated regional yield. No imported seed, store or unexplained food subsidy is counted.
The energy column uses explicit rough working assumptions: 6 kcal/g hazelnut kernels, 1.5 kcal/g dressed game or fish, and 2 kcal/g wet acorn meal. These are not extracted food-composition values (see R13 in Research Register). Wet meal composition is especially uncertain. Against an illustrative 2,500–3,500 kcal/day activity requirement, early days can be deficient and later entries are not all assured adequate. Cold, body size, illness, digestibility and work could change the balance. Internal conservation cannot prove long-term health or a realistic gathering rate.
Fuel is dry usable wood mass, excluding wet collected material. Collection and burn estimates are authored, without calorimeter or weather validation. Water columns count completed treatment and untreated drinking separately; evaporation and most other water uses are not modelled. Explicit additional processing-water estimates appear below and are not drinking intake. Initial untreated drinking is a survival risk, not a recommended procedure. Zero untreated intake means treatment was recorded, not independently certified.
Daily food continuity
Kernel use includes an explicitly recorded damp loss on Day 13. All retained fresh game is cooked and consumed on its catch day, including the limited 0.90 kg fox lot on Day 23. Discarded trimming is excluded from edible inputs. Acorns enter as 0.40 kg unprocessed input on Day 17, convert to 0.65 kg wet meal on Day 18 (water adds mass), and are eaten over Days 18–19. The input lot contributes no calories before processing.

Important events and limits

Day 3: first ignition; the fire kit needs continued maintenance. Stored heat is not permanent access to fire.
Days 4–5: first vessel heat trial fails, then repair permits recorded boiling. Day 9 wear interrupts treatment; Day 10 repairs restore it.
Day 7: the awl works. A needle attempt fails; a usable eyed needle follows on Day 12.
Days 9–10: the first rabbit pelt becomes a small carrying sling; the load test is under one kilogram.
Days 11–16: a small pot is shaped, dried, fired, cooled and rejected for leakage. It remains a non-food sample; no ceramic cooking asset is counted.
Days 4–20: the nettle batch is retted, processed in two halves, and partly made into cord. The first processing date is Day 16; elapsed time is twelve days, not a universal recipe.
Days 13–14 and 24: small hides become a pelvic pad and narrow shoulder panel. They do not amount to a winter coat.
Day 21: a wooden spindle bypasses ceramic success. A few metres of single yarn do not demonstrate a sustained productivity improvement.
Day 23: the damaged snare is removed. A limited fox meat lot is cooked and eaten, with additional work and fuel; its damaged pelt becomes a limited panel on Day 24.
Day 25: the first approach is rebuffed. Samples and the first spindle are abandoned during retreat, not accepted gifts. Day 26 records self-repair and planning, with no fibre exchange or shared teaching. No communal provisions or adoption are established.
Days 27–28: a replacement spindle is made. Two green dart candidates, a feather lot and an untested wooden atlatl remain distinct assets.

The earliest practical review should test food yield, bark-vessel reliability, heating-stone selection, fibre throughput and rawhide performance. Research Register records the evidence gaps; Civilisation Roadmap keeps later development tied to surplus and verified capabilities.
Current period and unfinished work
This ledger continues through Day 59. The original Days 1–28 entries retain the opening history and Day 28 state; later qualitative entries do not inherit these totals as current stock.
Days 29–35 establish a personal comparison record, an experimental green blunt dart, a small practice ground, a separately allocated bedding pad and retreat reconnaissance. At that week’s end, the new nettle batch and clay samples remain unfinished. No community supplies, hunting point, second completed dart, escape cache or supplied refuge are acquired in the opening week. The kernel reserve changes from 2.59 kg on Day 28 to 1.71 kg on Day 35; the dry-fuel stock ends that week at 19 kg.
Latest recorded ongoing states:

Two non-food fired comparison remnants are retained; short wetting result is not a watertight vessel, validated firing schedule or heat-cycle test.
Two raw comparison chips were softened in the water check and discarded; no duplicate raw set remains.
Footwear retains its limited improved dry trial; the next vessel, second suitable dart, supplied retreat and voluntary independent learning are future projects.
Both ignition kits and both tested bark vessels remain at the main camp; fallback bench is still unsupplied and unbuilt.
Dart A remains blunt unfletched and changing with moisture; B remains a bowed blank, feather stock unused. No second dart or hunting configuration.
Shelter, separate front/back grass screens, narrow left fox strip and plain rabbit crown pad retain their existing coverage; no waterproof or proven winter outfit.
Food buffer remains short; no stored meat, new game hide, accepted ceramic cooking vessel or community provisions.
