09_reference/valley-map.title: Valley Map
09_reference/valley-map.content:
Valley Map

This is the author’s spatial reference for the fictional valley in World, showing the camp and known landmarks at the end of Day 28. It is not a map the traveller has drawn, a real archaeological site, or a surveyed plan. Compass bearings, the arrangement of resource patches and the walking allowances below are new setting choices made on 3 October 2026. They consolidate the earlier descriptions without adding possessions or events.
The illustration provides the visual overview. The written relationships below govern continuity when an enlarged icon or decorative label is ambiguous. Terrain and ownership beyond the explored area remain unknown. R15 supports the broad regional landscape mosaic, not these particular locations.
Orientation and water
North is up. The larger river runs generally north to south through the eastern part of the map. The smaller stream runs west to east and joins it below the camp terrace. Both the traveller’s camp and the Neanderthal clearing are on the western side of the larger river. The established contact route requires no main-river crossing, boat, bridge or wading invention.
The camp sits north of the small stream, on a sheltered, drained terrace west of the main river. Ground around the shelter falls towards the southeast. Its entrance faces broadly southeast. The familiar Day 1 view looks out towards the east/southeast: the shelter is on the left and the valley drops away to the right. Other cameras can reverse screen positions while retaining these bearings.
The drinking-water seep is uphill and west/southwest of camp, at the upstream end of the small-stream route. The retting/rinsing pool is farther east and downstream of that collection point. Retting, clay work and dirty animal processing never move upstream of drinking collection. Appearance is not a water-safety test; Hot-Rock Boiling still applies.
The fish cage is at the accessible western margin of the larger river, just downstream of the tributary confluence. It is anchored in a shallow, locally sheltered margin and can be retrieved from stable footing. Its cylinder, inward entrance funnel and removable rear cap remain the design in Woven Fishing Trap. Neither an illustration nor this map creates a weir across the river. Day 22’s opposite-bank wolf is a transient sighting, not a permanent predator landmark.
Landmarks and travel allowances
These are provisional one-way allowances for a cautious, lightly loaded traveller from camp in ordinary daylight. They are author budgeting assumptions, not timings measured in the narrative. A loaded return, gathering, a trap check, a concealment pause or watching people adds time; poor weather and vigilance can lengthen every trip. Do not derive metres from the graphic.











































































LandmarkFixed relationshipOne-way allowance / useWater seepWest/southwest, upstream on the small-stream route5–10 minutes; collection and treatment are additional workRetting poolSouth/southwest, downstream of seep, before the confluence5–10 minutes; fibre work and rinsing remain separate from campFish trapSoutheast, western river margin below confluence10–15 minutes; checking does not guarantee a fishWillow and nettleAlong selected downstream tributary margins10–15 minutes to nearer stands; new harvesting needs inspectionClay bankTributary exposure southeast of camp, upstream of river confluence10–15 minutes; usable clay still requires testsGravel barEast/northeast, west bank of main river above confluence15–25 minutes; carrying stone back is slowerHazel and oakProtected patches west/northwest of camp10–25 minutes to nearer patches; the label denotes an area, not inexhaustible foodPine patchSouthwest, beyond the nearer stream margins15–25 minutes; fuel/resin gathering and transport add labourTrap circuitWestern terrestrial gathering area, near the nut patches10–20 minutes to the nearer trial sites, plus the circuit itselfRidge lookoutNorth of camp on the near/southern end of the rocky spur20–30 minutes; distant smoke can be seen beyond the ridgeMeeting groundNorthwest, beyond the spur’s western flank, short of the neighbouring living area40–60 minutes by the contact route; waiting and withdrawal are additionalNeanderthal clearingNorthwest of the ridge; same west-bank territory as the travellerBeyond the meeting ground; no permission to enter is assumedUpstream bendNorth/northeast along the west-bank river route35–50 minutes; Day 18’s old-antler excursion and carnivore-sign area
The trap-circuit label is deliberately an area marker. The three small deadfall trials have not acquired surveyed positions, and the damaged Day 23 snare is out of service. Do not read an active snare into the map. The upstream-bend label groups an excursion locality; it does not put the old antler at an active kill or establish a predator’s territory.
Resource icons show observed patches, not inventories, guaranteed seasonal yields or uncontested access. The dated narrative and Survival Ledger record actual acquisitions and later qualitative changes; historical quantities are not the current inventory.
Camp inset: fixed areas
The inset enlarges the camp and is not to scale with the main map. North remains up. It shows six areas already established by Day 28:

Shelter: northwest and upslope; a low leaf/bark/branch shelter under a thick fallen mossy limb. Preserve this structure rather than replacing it with a tent, hut or rock cave.
Craft spot: south of the shelter and west/upslope of the ordinary hearth. Its abrasion stone is a manageable ground-level stone, not a raised worktable.
Fire pit: southeast/downhill of the craft spot, outdoors and clear of the dry shelter. Leave an open access gap; no fire is brought beside the bedding for visual convenience.
Drying and processing: on the southern/southwestern dirty-material flank. The small drying frame and processing surface are separate from clean food and drinking-water handling.
Waste: farther southwest beyond that flank, on dry ground away from water collection and outside the stream bed. Future prose must account for removal and runoff, rather than treating a waste symbol as automatic sanitation.
Firing clearing: northeast of the ordinary hearth, separate bare ground well clear of shelter, drying frame and food work. It is the experimental outside firing place introduced on Day 14, not a kiln.

The inset’s miniature hearth and shelter symbols are exaggerated. They do not establish safe metre clearances. Future construction scenes must show an appropriate cleared buffer for their actual fuel, sparks and materials.
Contact route and retreat
Day 19’s smoke/firelight is observed beyond the ridge. Day 21’s cautious route follows the near slope to cover rather than entering the clearing. The main contact route leaves camp to the northwest, skirts the western flank of the spur, and reaches open meeting ground south of the Neanderthal clearing. It does not cut through their hearth/work area.
The concealed stopping-place for the traveller’s spear lies on that approach, south of and short of the meeting ground. He retrieves it on the retreat in Day 25. The map’s dotted line marks a remembered walking route, not an engineered road or safe corridor. The clearing’s occupants can see open ground and may control access to nearby resources. Nothing here guarantees neutral land.
No secondary shelter, supplied emergency cache or atlatl practice range has yet been built. The approved Month Two Outline will require choosing those sites through observation and work. A future range must have a clear flight/retrieval area and backstop, directed away from the river, contact route and occupied camps. A retreat site must be independently reachable and supplied; the map cannot grant it for free.
Use in later writing and illustration
For each new scene, name its location, compass view, slope/water direction and objects actually present at that moment. Check travel and return allowances before assigning the day’s work. At the camp, retain the inset relationships even when some features are outside the frame. At other locations, do not import camp furniture to make the scene recognisable.
Keep the landscape a mosaic of sheltered woods, open ground and rocky relief. Map ornament does not imply continuous forest, modern cultivation or a medieval settlement. The neighbouring clearing icon represents a maintained hearth and working ground; it specifies no permanent architecture or full group population.
Add a dated update when a fixed object or route changes. Keep the Day 28 map as a historical state; do not quietly draw completed Month 2 facilities into it. The machine-readable layout and full generation prompt are stored in _Artwork/maps/location-layout.json and the full original and correction prompts, _Artwork/maps/valley-day-28-v1-prompt.txt and _Artwork/maps/valley-day-28-v2-prompt.txt. Their normalised anchors express relative placement, not ground measurements. See Illustration Continuity for scene and character rules.
Dated additions after the illustrated state
The main picture remains a Day 28 map. Separate later Survival scenes and place plates illustrate the dated additions without changing that historical overview. The written bearings remain authoritative.

Day 29 selection / Day 30 preparation: the small practice ground lies west/southwest of camp, above the tributary and short of the western trap circuit. Casts face west into a local earth bank, with the river and contact route outside the intended flight line. The site requires reinspection; markers do not establish permanent safe access.
Day 33 reconnaissance: an alternative bench southwest of the pine patch has natural rock screening. The route follows western ground upstream of the seep’s head, then turns south along higher ground, avoiding a main-river crossing. Allow roughly 35–50 minutes one way in ordinary daylight, plus the return and inspection. Water is not established at the bench; it remains an unsupplied candidate, with no constructed shelter or cache.

These additions are new authored locations and time allowances, not points which were secretly explored on Day 28. Preserve the camp inset’s fixed arrangement while repairing the roof or adding a small pad to its existing bed.
Days 36–40: observed use without a new installation
The fish cage receives a rear-closure repair at its existing western river margin below the confluence. Day 37’s watchers stand north of the west-directed short practice line, and one local adult casts his own spear into the bank after the traveller stands clear. This is a temporary event, not a second practice range or new camp.
Day 39 finds people gathering at the western edge of the familiar nut circuit, short of the spur contact route. Their warning leads to withdrawal; it does not define a surveyed territorial boundary or move the neighbouring clearing. All craft and pelt work retain the camp inset’s clean/dirty arrangement. No refuge or cache exists at the fallback bench through Day 40. The Day 28 graphic remains a historical overview.
Dated shelter work: Days 41–45
The Day 28 artwork remains the early-state overview. Day 41 assesses the existing northwest camp shelter. Ten selected light members are gathered on Day 43. The Day 44–45 north/east return framework and partial cover rebuild the same footprint, preserving the southeast entrance, the retained limb and the old occupied side. No fire, craft, processing, firing or water feature moves. See Traveller’s Camp and Framed Debris Shelter for the dated construction state; this addition does not redraw the original map into a completed winter camp.
Dated observations and work: Days 46–50
The original map remains the Day 28 overview. The later shelter overlap and offset entrance bundle stay in the northwest camp footprint with a clear southeast mouth. The Day 47 canid visit is transient on the southwest dirty flank; the cleared sight gap is not a permanent predator territory or new road. Day 48 follows deer sign within the western gathering terrain, short of the occupied nut patch/contact route. It adds no new named site, camp, river crossing, surveyed deer trail or supplied fallback bench.
Dated addition: Western Overhang — Days 60–64
Western Overhang is newly inspected on Day 60 and occupied on Day 61. It lies west/northwest and uphill of the old camp near the southern foot of the rocky spur, facing southeast on the same west side of the main river. The known seep remains southeast along contour ground. The place note defines provisional route allowances and the new local working arrangement.
This addition does not move the old Day 28 illustrated landmarks or add the overhang to that historical picture. It is distinct from the unsupplied fallback bench. The old camp is abandoned as the occupied home after movable equipment transfers; its dirty drying frame and rejected pot remain. The trap stays at its riverside anchor. The new overhang inset records the arrangement through Day 64, not a measured survey or completed winter dwelling.
View the separate Western Overhang inset through Day 64. Its icons identify working areas; the written place description governs geography and does not treat icons as new catches or inventory. The original Day 28 map image remains unchanged.

The revised trap set and deer observations remain within the established west-bank terrestrial circuit and gathering terrain, short of the contact approach. The solo result occurs within a manageable return of the overhang; no main-river crossing, surveyed deer trail, new named hunting locality or cache is established. 09_reference/vault-maintenance.title: Vault Maintenance
09_reference/vault-maintenance.content:
Vault Maintenance
Edit the source, then derive the views
Daily frontmatter contains demonstrated capabilities, assets, food lots, fuel, drinking-water quantities and work estimates. Reference frontmatter contains default requirements, alternatives and improvements. Do not edit the generated tables to change history.
Use these commands from the vault folder, in order:
python tools/update_views.py
python tools/validate_vault.py
python tools/export_context.py
The tools require Python 3 and PyYAML. Both were available during this revision. The root combine_files_full.bat performs the same update-and-export workflow when double-clicked; combine_files_parts.bat also creates text parts. Export validates the vault before replacing the previous full context.
update_views.py writes first-recorded demonstration dates into capability pages and derives four views: Survival Ledger, Acquired, Dependency Register and Topic Index. Survival Ledger retains the historical Days 1–59 calculations and later qualitative changes; historical totals are not a current inventory. The duplicate first-month view has been retired and is no longer generated. Preserve their logic in the generator if changing their prose. validate_vault.py reads without editing. It checks category folders, subtypes, domains, primary tags, metadata, duplicate YAML keys, links and heading targets, local illustrations, prerequisite cycles, demonstration order, food and asset conservation, fuel balances and work-hour sums.
After selecting a plate or moving an illustrated page, run python tools/update_artwork_galleries.py to refresh the original generation-batch galleries and the current equipment, skill, process and structure galleries. Original PNGs and full prompts stay in their generation folders; current page links follow the category organisation.
These checks do not certify species identification, material performance, the realism of labour estimates or historical presence. Read Research Register and the note’s evidence limits before treating a procedure as publishable.
Lunar reviews and page moves
Use Page Scope and Organisation when combining variants and object-specific assembly. Preserve stable canonical IDs, old name/path aliases, real image assets and exact historical prompts. The 4 October migration manifest records merged IDs and paths; original galleries use their actual recorded image rather than substituting a merged page’s primary image.
tools/lunar_calendar.py defines an approximate fictional epoch and milestone rhythm. update_views.py fills daily model phase fields and cutoff-specific reflection snapshots. validate_vault.py checks phases, reflection cutoffs/snapshots and place references as well as capabilities. Write/refine reflection prose deliberately after source-day changes; the table’s regeneration does not rewrite the judgement. No review creates another ledger day.
Exports and recovery
The full context includes Markdown only from numbered vault folders, in natural order. It excludes tools, Obsidian settings, archives and old exports. Split outputs are .txt files in _ContextExports, outside the content graph. INDEX.txt identifies the current set; old extra parts may remain and should not be included unless listed. A single unusually long note can exceed the approximate part size.
The initial prose archive is _RevisionArchive/2026-10-01-before-revision.zip. The category revision snapshot is _RevisionArchive/2026-10-02-before-category-revision.zip; it includes notes, helper scripts, artwork records, workspace settings and PNG fingerprints. The PNG files themselves remain unchanged in the vault. Inspect individual files to recover earlier prose; do not extract an archive over the working vault unless deliberately restoring that state. Revision Record describes the scope and choices, and the category migration map records former and current paths.
Adding a day or a capability
Use Category Specification and Page Templates. Give each note a unique stable id, one primary type/tag, a valid subtype and at least one recognised domain. Classify the subject rather than its complexity, history or development state. The category definitions and domain vocabulary are in tools/category_model.py. Use real filenames or aliases in wiki-links. Keep survival days consecutive, and use stable lot and asset keys. Positive events introduce stock; negative events use, lose or gift it. Zero-change asset events record condition of an existing object.
When moving or renaming a page, preserve the stable ID and useful old names/path aliases, update ordinary Markdown and gallery links, and rebase its relative image path. Regenerate views and exports. A category change does not create a new physical asset, demonstrate a missing skill or validate a process.
Food disposition is collected, consumed, processed or lost. Consumption reduces stock and contributes to the explicit energy model. Converting acorns adds a processed wet output separately; water gain is not additional food energy. Fresh game lots use catch-specific names such as rabbit-day29 and are consumed the same day in the first-month model.
demonstrates refers to the traveller’s own limited capability instance. Structures join that graph; places use locations_used, locations_observed and dated location_events rather than demonstration or stock events. community_demonstrates records observations or shared trials separately. If a listed default prerequisite has not been demonstrated, either provide the missing work or describe and encode the actual alternative route. Do not invent an acquisition date to silence the check.
A later period needs its own accounting scope. Change the same-day game rule only alongside a researched preservation method and storage model; change the daily narrative scale when seasons and projects become the useful unit.

10_mission/mission-coordination.title: Mission Coordination
10_mission/mission-coordination.content:
Mission Coordination
The mission depends on people being able and willing to reproduce, maintain and extend capabilities. These social subjects follow the same categories as the physical handbook: a person’s ability is a skill, while coordinated arrangements are systems.






























SubjectPrimary categoryRole in the missionCommunication and ExchangeSkillEstablish shared meaning, observe responses and negotiate cooperationTeaching and Knowledge PreservationTechnology — systemDevelop learning and preservation that can survive the traveller’s absenceMeasurement and RecordsTechnology — systemMaintain shared references and observations that support comparison and replicationSanitation and Camp HygieneTechnology — systemCoordinate water, waste, handling and maintenance across the camp
These are linked capabilities, rather than duplicate copies in the Mission folder. Their pages describe limited demonstrations, unresolved questions and later requirements. Category Specification explains the conceptual split, Topic Index groups the related pages, and Civilisation Roadmap carries the mission through surplus, institutions, industry and space systems.
Winter before cooperation — 23 October 2026
The user directs December to remain a solitary winter. Moon Four Outline develops independent clothing, food and useful production; Flora and Fauna guides seasonal opportunities. Existing limited contact does not become standing provisioning or a learning programme. Sustained cooperation and knowledge transfer remain a spring direction, with no new community demonstrations recorded by this plan.

_artwork/skills/gallery.title: gallery
_artwork/skills/gallery.content:
Skills illustrations
Current illustrated pages; the original PNGs and prompts retain their generation history. All manual plates.
Atlatl Throwing
Skills page
Three small separated outline side-profile figures show SAME ordinary human in three positions, with NO overlapping ghostlimbs: balanced setup, coordinated forward movement, follow-through. Each has exactly two arms/two legs; modest natural clothing. Slender wooden atlatl with small supported spur engaging rear seat of long BLUNT UNFLETCHED dart at setup; appropriate overarm throw with body turn, later lever rises, projectile clears hook. No giant crook, fletching, bow or spearhead. Labels ‘BALANCE’, ‘COORDINATE’, ‘FOLLOW THROUGH’. Conceptual motion plate not mastered narrative action. Dashed path only beyond release.

Basic Foraging
Skills page
Close still-life technique study of a whole hazel twig with rounded toothed leaves, intact husked hazelnuts and opened nut showing cream kernel, plus hands sorting sound nuts from cracked dark moulding rejected one into separate bark scraps. Label ‘IDENTIFY WHOLE PLANT’, ‘EDIBLE PORTION’, ‘COUNT PROCESSING’. Positive identified hazel teachingexample, not generic edible wild plant key. No tasting unknown leaves, mushrooms, rich harvest heap or modern measuring scale.

Basic Spear Fishing
Skills page
Single educational water-refraction cross-section, no catching scene. Person simplified only at bank with bare feet on STABLE DRY GROUND, wooden-pointed spear tip near surface, water shallow and slow. Real fish clearly drawn below surface; dotted pale duplicate ABOVE real fish labelled ‘APPARENT POSITION’. Light ray bends at surface consistently; aim ray points below apparent image toward realfish. Labels ‘STABLE FOOTING’, ‘REFRACTION’, ‘REAL POSITION’. No impaled fish, deep wading or boat.

Basic Thatching
Skills page
Close side-section of sloped small timber shelter framework. Hands placing an upper grass bundle course over the top of lower course; clearly downhill direction with a few blue water arrows on TOP of outer thatch leading down off eave, never into roof. Two courses overlapping like shingles. Label ‘WORK UPWARD’, ‘OVERLAPPING COURSES’, ‘KEEP OPENINGS CLEAR’. No indoor hearth or metal roof.

Beam Fleshing
Skills page
A conceptual clean supported skin fold over a smooth stable rounded beam, illustrating control rather than a separate owned skin.

Berry Foraging
Skills page
One botanical bramble twig bearing recognisable clustered blackberries with toothed compound leaves and thorns. Hand selecting one sound ripe black berry, small clean bark tray below, separate squashed sample isolated. Labels ‘CONFIRM THE PLANT’, ‘SOUND FRUIT’, ‘SMALL CLEAN LOT’. No generic redberry edibility code or invented exact specieskey, plentiful basket, cooking apparatus.

Bifacial Knapping
Skills page
A blank and opposite faces of a rough biface, emphasising work on both faces.

Bow Drill Fire
Skills page
Side three-quarter close technique study: dry flat hearth board socket near edge with V-notch joining socket to outside edge and small bark ember catcher UNDER notch. Vertical spindle held at top by bearing block in operator hand; other hand holds curved wooden bow, single cord wraps spindle once. Foot braces board away from notch; bearing wrist supported against shin, bow path unobstructed. No flame; tiny dark dust mound at notch. Inset sustained small ember separate from smoke icon. Labels ‘STABLE BEARING’, ‘DUST NOTCH’, ‘EMBER CATCHER’. Show at most cropped lower body, two hands, one foot.

Bow Shooting
Skills page
Bare-handed inspection of the same recovered plain practice arrow after the short trials; both warming covers set together on clean bark and the bow already put away unstrung.

Clay Drying and Inspection
Skills page
An intact greenware pot and a separate witness-section comparison illustrating drying judgement.

Communication and Exchange
Skills page
Two clothed schematic human adults several paces apart, one open palm held low and the other calm raised stop palm, both normal upright anatomy. A small neutral wooden sample lies beside first adult, NOT passed hand to hand. Broken arc on ground conveys distance; open retreat arrow away from encounter. Labels ‘OBSERVE DISTANCE’, ‘RESPECT REFUSAL’, ‘SHARED MEANING’. No speech transcript, hand shaking, barter piles or celebration. Universal reference skill, not invented trading in current story.

Cordage Testing
Skills page
A wet/dry fibre-line comparison with a smooth support and a close texture inset; no rated strength or restraint rig.

Crayfish Gathering
Skills page
Conceptual assessment plate, NOT a local occurrence claim: isolated generic freshwater crayfish in natural ochre/blue labelled ‘CONFIRM SPECIES’. Secondary shallow-water bank section, hand kept ABOVE rock rather than reaching blindly beneath it; footprint on dry stablebank. Small closed empty bark specimen tray. Labels ‘CHECK LOCAL PRESENCE’, ‘STABLE FOOTING’, ‘DO NOT REACH BLINDLY’. No catch, meal, eating, red boiled shell or predicted yield.

Edible Plant Identification
Skills page
Assessment plate with one whole neutral botanical specimen drawn roots/stem/leaves/fruit together and three enlarged feature callouts: leaf attachment, flower structure, fruit. None labelled as edible species, no taste action. Add simple paired outlines of similar plants with one discriminating feature highlighted. Labels ‘WHOLE ORGANISM’, ‘COMPARE FEATURES’, ‘CHECK LOOKALIKES’. No universal toxicity code, identified edible mushroom, taste test or one-feature safety rule.

Environmental Observation
Skills page
Hand-drawn conceptual terrain study with small shelter icon on drained highground, stream line downhill, open escape arrow and tiny footprint/smoke sign marked question near ridge. NOT literal surveyed valley map: use no compass scale or numbered travel distances. Insets a hand checking soil dampness and three simple repeated observations. Labels ‘OBSERVE’, ‘COMPARE’, ‘REVISIT’. No certainty about owners or motives, second suppliedcamp.

Fletching
Skills page
Bare-handed binding of two modest feather vanes to the one existing practice arrow, with both hand pockets set aside.

Flint Knapping Basics
Skills page
Close hands on well-supported knappablecore with a small roundedhammerstone poised above exposed edge; intended removal path away from handandleg. Two isolated flakes and a small hinged removal comparison. Navy leaderlines labels ‘SOUND PLATFORM’, ‘CONTROLLED STRIKE’, ‘INSPECT REMOVAL’. No metalchisels, huge perfect handaxe, pressureflakingantler, exactuniversalangle or cutskin. Fingers kept behind workingedge.

Hand Drill Fire
Skills page
Conceptual alternative: slender straight dry wooden spindle vertical in a notched hearth board on ground; two open palms facing each other on opposite sides of spindle, arrows showing rotation and downward pressure. Cropped knee helps brace board; small catcher beneath notch. No bow, cord or bearing block. No flame or guaranteed ember. Labels ‘ROTATE’, ‘CONTROL PRESSURE’, ‘EMBER NOT SMOKE’. Generic prepared wood, no identifiable poisonous stems.

Hand-Line Fishing
Skills page
Attending a hand-held fishing line from firm dry near-bank ground, with the existing small hand net within reach before a take.

Hunting Approach
Skills page
A field-manual study of observation, screened approach and a clear return route.

Knots - Primitive Set
Skills page
An accurately traced natural two-strand cord with ONE simple overhand stopper knot enlarged as main study: rope doubles into loop, free end passes once through the loop and is drawn into a single overhand knot. Small inset shows generous free tail under low test tension and witness mark for slipping. NOT a bowline, snare, decorative tangle or detached rope ring. Labels ‘DRESS THE KNOT’, ‘LEAVE A TAIL’, ‘CHECK FOR CREEP’. Only ONE knot illustrated; page lists other knots in prose.

Knotted Netting
Skills page
Small regular knotted mesh hung from a starting cord, with a smooth wooden gauge at the unfinished row.

Measurement and Records
Skills page
Hands compare one plain notched wooden reference rod to a second short workpiece, starting ends aligned on bark mat. Separate small bark slip shows two groups of simple unconnected tally strokes. Spare small similar kernellots not largefoodheap. Labels ‘SAME REFERENCE’, ‘ALIGN THE ENDS’, ‘RECORD FAILURES’. No Arabic numerals, SIcalibration, metal ruler, modernnotebook, balanceorcommunalstandards.

Medicinal Plant Assessment
Skills page
Quiet research-assessment plate: neutral botanical sprig, small unfilled bark tray and bark record slip with unnumbered simple marks. Three separated leader areas ‘IDENTITY’, ‘PREPARATION’, ‘EVIDENCE’. Small hand holds sprig for inspection, no mortarful remedy, infusion dose, wound, treatment or sterile claim. Distinguish consideration from application; no medical symbols promising cure.

Mushroom Foraging
Skills page
Reference identification framework: two isolated non-labelled generic mushrooms, one shown complete with cap, stem, gills, intact base and substrate; small enlarged detail of underside and base. Emphasise observation and uncertainty with labels ‘WHOLE SPECIMEN’, ‘CHECK THE BASE’, ‘LEAVE UNCERTAIN’. No green edible checkmark, safety diagnosis, tasting, harvested mushroom basket or safe-versus-poison speciespair. No meal.

Mussel Harvesting
Skills page
Two closed generic freshwater bivalve research specimens in isolation, with a partly exposed one on shallow sediment inset; observer’s foot on stable dry bank, no barefoot sweeping. Short labels ‘IDENTIFY SPECIES’, ‘ASSESS WATER SOURCE’, ‘KEEP SEPARATE’. Small clean empty bark research tray, not cooked mussels or meal. No universal edible checkmarks or assertion heating removes toxins.

Projectile Testing
Skills page
Top-down small generic experimental ground, NOT surveyed valleymap. Clear short start position faces broad EARTH BANK backstop, tiny dispersed dart landing marks with two separate trial groups in dusty blue/coral. A slim blunt unfletched dart and separate small thrower lie isolated at edge. One bark tally slip has simple strokes. Labels ‘SAME START’, ‘RECORD MISSES’, ‘CHANGE ONE FACTOR’. No speed/energy/range numbers, bullseye victory, people in path or pointed huntingdart.

Retreat Planning
Skills page
Conceptual route-and-load plate: small primary shelter icon and an EMPTY natural rock-screened bench, dotted alternative walking route stays on SAME SIDE of stream without crossing deep water. Modest essentials isolated: wooden-pointed spear, stoneflake, bow-drillkit, smallbarkvessel and tiny nutportion with existing pouch, no backpack or extra duplicatekit. Labels ‘KEEP AN EXIT’, ‘TEST THE CARRY’, ‘UNSUPPLIED SITE’. No fortifiedrefuge, cache, defensive trap, guaranteeorattack.

Scavenging
Skills page
Main isolated worn old RED-DEER SHED ANTLER fragment examined by one hand above dry grass, blunt cut base and branched tines recognisable, no skull attached. Secondary faint ground-sign inset has carnivoreprint and withdrawal arrow. Labels ‘DETACHED MATERIAL’, ‘CHECK CONDITION’, ‘LEAVE FRESH PREDATOR SIGN’. No active kill, meat pile, predator confrontation or stolen hominid equipment.

Shelter Construction
Skills page
Checking a light fork-and-rail bearing from outside before adding cover.

Simple Coiling and Weaving
Skills page
Two separate side-by-side basketry construction studies, clearly distinguish mechanisms. LEFT small spiral soft grass foundation with individual stitches linking new outer coil to preceding one; bone awl in a gap not puncturing thick wood. RIGHT upright slender willow stakes with ONE flexible working strand passing alternately in front/behind, open unfinished wall. Labels ‘COILED FOUNDATION’, ‘JOIN EACH COIL’, ‘STAKE AND STRAND’. No net or twining.

Simple Cordage
Skills page
Macro close study of two fibre bundles in hands being reverse wrapped into two-ply line. Each bundle’s own twist direction opposes the direction they wrap around each other. Use curved arrows one kind around bundle and opposite larger arrow around pair, physically traceable continuous fibres. Completed short line hangs below pinch point. Secondary inset shows staggered overlapping fibre joins at DIFFERENT positions in two strands. Labels ‘TWIST EACH BUNDLE’, ‘WRAP OPPOSITE’, ‘STAGGER JOINS’. No spindle or loom.

Simple Hafting
Skills page
A supported stone-and-wood joint with mechanical binding clear of the working edge.

Small Game Butchery
Skills page
Separated work zones: at left a clean slate with small neutral-coloured meat portions and a stone flake, at right one small fur pelt laid flat and a separate dirty scrap bowl. Cropped hands carefully draw a blunt scraper across the pelt’s cream underside, no exposed viscera, blood or carcass wound. Labels ‘CLEAN FOOD’, ‘PELT WORK’, ‘CLEAN IMPLEMENTS’. Illustrate contamination control and limited yield, not a slaughter scene.

Spear Throwing
Skills page
Two separate side-profile motion studies of the same robust upright human wearing modest simple skin clothing: balanced start and coordinated hand release. Correct human anatomy no overlapping ghost arms. LONG stone-pointed spear with knapped head bound into wooden shaft, cast BY HAND, no atlatl, bow or dart fletching. One tiny separate grouping diagram not numericalrange. Labels ‘COORDINATE THE BODY’, ‘CONTROL RELEASE’, ‘RETRIEVE AND INSPECT’. Generic explanatory skill, not protagonist competence or species-strength scale.

Spindle Plying
Skills page
Two separate single threads meeting at a controlled junction and wrapping into one plied line above a wooden spindle.

Stitching
Skills page
Close main study of two small overlapping pale rawhide scraps with widely spaced pre-pierced holes away from edges. A short bone eyed needle pulling one thin natural thread through both layers; a few completed even stitches beside it, needle fully separate from finger. Small detail shows hole too close to edge with tear compared to sound margin. Labels ‘PRE-PIERCE’, ‘EVEN TENSION’, ‘SOUND MARGIN’. No industrial thread, steel needle or modern fabric.

Stone Selection
Skills page
Two contrasted isolated stone samples: rounded tough percussor cobble and fine-grained core with one small clean conchoidal flake scar and separate sharpflake. Third small visibly crackedweathered rejectedcobble. A hand turns sound sample, not striking. Labels ‘PERCUSSOR’, ‘TEST FRACTURE’, ‘REJECT CRACKS’. No claimedhighgradeflint fromcolouralone, polishedgem, metaltool or hugecollection.

Tillering
Skills page
Taking small shavings from the belly of the same unstrung wooden body between low-deflection comparisons.

Tracking
Skills page
Three successive hoof-print pairs in soft soil, direction arrows along trackway, one weather-softened edge shown enlarged beside fresh-looking edge without claiming exact age. Small hands use plain uncalibrated reference stick for comparison. Labels ‘PATTERN’, ‘SUBSTRATE’, ‘CORROBORATE’. No certain species diagnosis from singleprint, timestamps, metricruler or guaranteedtrapcatch.

Tripod Lashing
Skills page
Three parallel wooden poles bound by several wraps around all three near aligned tops; close enlarged inset shows TWO frapping paths running in spaces between poles tightening wraps, not random wound cord. A small lower-right secondary study of same three poles spread into three-legged tripod with load arrow falling INSIDE triangular footprint. Exactly THREE poles and feet, no fourth. Labels ‘WRAPS’, ‘FRAPPING TURNS’, ‘LOAD INSIDE BASE’. Natural fibre cord no metal fasteners.

Twining
Skills page
Large macro technical study of FOUR upright pale willow strip foundations and EXACTLY TWO continuous working cords, one dusty blue and one muted coral for teaching distinction. The two cords CROSS in each space BETWEEN neighbouring foundations and change front/back position, enclosing each foundation, not an ordinary single-strand over/under weave. One completed row only, enlarged gap detail. Labels ‘TWO WORKING ELEMENTS’, ‘CROSS BETWEEN’, ‘FOUNDATIONS’. No loom, knots at every crossing or finished blanket.

index.title: Humanity Handbook
index.content:
A traveller arrives in northern Iberia around 40,000 years ago, carrying humanity’s knowledge in memory and nothing else. The handbook follows the work of turning that knowledge into practical capabilities, from the first shelter and fire to a society capable of planetary defence.
Start with The Mission and the Handbook, then the setting and the valley map.
Read the story
Begin the story →
The story follows one person’s trials, failures and discoveries. The reference pages describe the materials, skills, equipment and systems behind them.
Explore the handbook

The story — Follow the traveller from arrival, day by day.
Reflections — Read the arrival appraisal and milestone reviews.
Materials — Explore natural and manufactured stocks.
Skills — Find the practical abilities needed to make progress.
Tools and equipment — Browse objects, clothing, containers and machinery.
Structures and places — Explore construction and the places in the story.
Processes and systems — Connect resources, skills and equipment into working systems.
Historical eras — Use history as orientation for the route ahead.
Reference — Find the ledgers, dependencies and research notes.
The mission — Follow cooperation and the longer route to planetary defence.
